You are a worker executing exactly one step of the Fortress clean-ladder rebuild: **step B2** (generated-source determinism).

Your execution contract is the plan file: read `/home/user/fortress/explorations/rebuild-plan.md` in full before doing anything — especially "Worktree and environment mechanics", "Gate definitions", the "### Base block" intro, your step **B2**, the "Execution checklist", and "Known risks / stop conditions". The plan is authoritative; do not improvise beyond it.

Constants:
- Clean worktree: `/home/user/fortress-clean`, branch `clean-ladder` (tip = B1's .gitignore commit `6abefcb88`). Rebuild commits go ONLY on this branch. Do NOT push clean-ladder for this step (pushes start at B3).
- Working-branch checkout: `/home/user/fortress`, branch `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr` — used ONLY for the checklist tick.
- Reference commits (`3c4dcdabc`, `c4c90f936`, `760f7ea2a`, graft `8fe1daa8f`, tip `eb7e91859`) are reachable in this shared repo; inspect with `git show`/`git diff` from either worktree.
- Every commit message ends with exactly this footer (last two lines):

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX

- Never include any model identifier in committed content or messages. Commit messages carry the full reasoning.

Your duties for B2:
1. First run the plan's precondition check: verify the base's generator sources match the graft's (`git diff a874948ac 8fe1daa8f -- ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen` must be empty — note `ProjectFortress/astgen/` is the schema dir, NOT the generators). If not empty, that is a deviation: report and stop.
2. Bring the three generator sources under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/` to their `eb7e91859` content (this folds in `3c4dcdabc` + `c4c90f936` + `760f7ea2a` as the plan explains). Identify which files those three commits touched (`git show --stat` on each) and take exactly those files at tip content.
3. Apply the TWO build.xml hunks from `3c4dcdabc` (see `git show 3c4dcdabc -- ProjectFortress/build.xml`): the makeAST `replaceregexp` normalizing astgen.jar-emitted headers, and the buildparser Rats! date normalization. Apply them to the trunk build.xml in the clean worktree (anchors verified present in trunk); take ONLY those two hunks — nothing else from that commit's build.xml diff if more exists, and no other build.xml changes.
4. Self-verify: `git diff --stat` shows only the intended files (generator sources + build.xml); the generator files are byte-identical to their `eb7e91859` versions (`git diff eb7e91859 -- <paths>` empty for those files); the two build.xml hunks are present and nothing else changed in build.xml (compare against `a874948ac:ProjectFortress/build.xml`). No build is run — B2's gate is deferred to B4 by the plan.
5. Commit on `clean-ladder` as ONE commit with a reasoned message (explain the determinism goal, the three folded source commits, the two build.xml hunks, and that proof comes at B4's double regeneration) + footer. Do NOT push.
6. Tick the B2 checkbox in `## Execution checklist` of `/home/user/fortress/explorations/rebuild-plan.md` (mark `[x]`, append the short SHA), commit that one-file change on the working branch in `/home/user/fortress` (short message + same footer), then push: `git push origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`, then `git push origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr:main` (standing orders; retry on network failure only, 2s/4s/8s/16s).
7. Report tersely: precondition result, files changed, B2 SHA, tick SHA, deviations (a deviation is NOT yours to resolve — report and stop).

Your final text is your report to the coordinator, not prose for a human.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- algorithmic-art: Creating algorithmic art using p5.js with seeded randomness and interactive parameter exploration. Use this when users request creating art using code, generative art, algorithmic art, flow fields, or particle systems. Create original algorithmic art rather than copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
- doc-coauthoring: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- theme-factory: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.
- web-artifacts-builder: Suite of tools for creating elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts using modern frontend web technologies (React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui). Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

1	# Clean-ladder rebuild plan
2	
3	Status: **approved for execution** (Pavol, 2026-08-22); independently
4	adversarially reviewed 2026-08-22, all findings folded in. This file is the
5	execution contract: it is written to be executable cold, after any number
6	of context compactions or container losses, by reading this file alone plus
7	the referenced commits.
8	
9	## Goal
10	
11	Replace the first ascent — pluckyporcupine's graft overlay plus the 63
12	revival commits on top of it — with a curated linear history built directly
13	on the pure 2012 trunk. Each modernization rung is one gated commit whose
14	message carries the full reasoning. The new branch is `clean-ladder`
15	(temporary name; Pavol renames it to `main` via the GitHub UI when done).
16	The current working branch `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr` is untouched and
17	keeps the full first-ascent record.
18	
19	Primary sources this plan distills:
20	
21	- `explorations/modernization-plan.md` § "Clean-ladder rebuild: hindsight
22	  ordering (2026-08-21)" — the lessons and the first-draft ordering.
23	- The working branch's commit history (all hashes below are on
24	  `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`, tip `eb7e91859` at time of writing;
25	  70 commits in `a874948ac..eb7e91859`, every one either transplanted,
26	  re-executed, or deliberately left behind by this plan). Pin bumped
27	  2026-08-23 from `3595f511d`: the six commits in between touched only
28	  spec-land (E4's cherry-pick), this plan file and `protocol.md` (not
29	  transplanted), and the README (E1 is a content snapshot, not a
30	  cherry-pick, so the link fix rides in via the pin — no squash needed).
31	- Branch `spike/scala-upgrade`, single commit `73f598202` on top of
32	  `a874948ac` — the executed de-risking spike for B3 (2026-08-23): the
33	  exact five-file revival diff, gated where it lands (testFast 1,377
34	  tests / 47 suites fully green; testSystem 382 tests with exactly the
35	  seven known 2012 failures). B3 re-lands this commit.
36	
37	## Decisions already made by Pavol (do not re-litigate)
38	
39	- Branch name `clean-ladder`, pushed to `origin clean-ladder`. Temporary;
40	  renamed to `main` later by Pavol.
41	- Exhibit block **first**, ladder after. The kickoff commit is a README
42	  whose only ladder-dependent sentence is deferred to a closing amendment.
43	- **No CI in the base block.** CI stays a goal on the working branch only
44	  (`explorations/ci/gate.yml` parked; Pavol pushes it much later — token
45	  lacks `workflows` scope). This deliberately overrides the hindsight
46	  section's item 10 / rung 0.9.
47	- The test-suite speedup (working-branch commits `4b1e500ca` +
48	  `e0f550094`) **is** part of the base block, gated once against a
49	  full-speed run, placed after the tree is fully green so its gate has a
50	  meaningful baseline.
51	- Not transplanted (stay working-branch-only): `explorations/protocol.md`,
52	  `explorations/repo-internals.md`, `explorations/modernization-plan.md`,
53	  `explorations/readme-plan.md`, `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`,
54	  `explorations/test-suite-speedup.md`,
55	  `explorations/swift-vs-fortress-explainer.md`, `explorations/ci/`,
56	  `research/README.md`, both Steele talk extracts,
57	  `research/extracts/fortress-websites-wayback.md`, and this plan file
58	  itself. Clean-branch `research/` holds **only** `authorship.md`.
59	  `CLAUDE.md` is also not transplanted for now (it references
60	  working-branch-only files); a clean-branch variant is a later decision.
61	- Commit conventions (from `modernization-plan.md` § Conventions +
62	  protocol): messages carry the full reasoning; every commit ends with
63	  the footer
64	  `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` +
65	  `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LjDz79rDLErtnSKpovMDpX`;
66	  **no model identifiers** anywhere in committed artifacts.
67	- Pavol decides what gets committed; this plan was reviewed and approved as
68	  a whole, so execution proceeds commit by commit without further
69	  per-commit approval, but any *deviation* discovered during execution is
70	  reported back before improvising.
71	
72	## Base point
73	
74	Branch from `a874948acb5b4b6aa7791e8d735657437910d879` — the final original
75	trunk commit (karl.naden, 2012-08-31 15:12:23 -0400, "initial writeup of
76	instantiation stuff using small theory instead of welterweight"). Verified
77	in HEAD lineage.
78	
79	Facts about this tree that the hindsight ordering (written against the
80	*graft* tree) got wrong, verified 2026-08-22:
81	
82	- **Scala 2.9.0**, not 2.10.7. `ProjectFortress/third_party/scala/` holds
83	  `scala-{compiler,library}-2.9.0.jar`. The 2.10.7 toolchain arrived with
84	  the graft overlay — which this rebuild *replaces*, so the migration is
85	  re-landed as the spike-verified minimal commit (B3 below). Spike
86	  baseline check (2026-08-23): the untouched trunk does **not** build on
87	  JDK 8 — Scala 2.9.0's classfile parser cannot read the Java 8 rt.jar
88	  ("bad constant pool tag 18" loading `java.util.Comparator`, 116 cascade
89	  errors), and no JDK 7 is installable on Ubuntu 24.04 — confirming that
90	  B1/B2 land un-gated by design, not by neglect.
91	- **No vendored BCEL.** Trunk's
92	  `runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:27` imports the *JDK-internal*
93	  `com.sun.org.apache.bcel.internal.generic.INVOKEINTERFACE` (satisfied by
94	  rt.jar on JDK 8; dead code — sole use site line 212 compares against the
95	  ASM `Opcodes` constant). The graft repointed that import to
96	  `org.apache.bcel.*` and vendored BCEL 6.2 (378 files + bcel.jar) to
97	  satisfy it. So there is no "delete BCEL" base commit here, and BCEL
98	  never lands at all; the dead import line is deleted at R2 (what
99	  `2f1fdbf2e` eventually did), where JDK 11's removal of
100	  `com.sun.org.apache.bcel.internal` makes it an error. On JDK 8 it is
101	  merely a warning — spike-verified: the base block gates green with the
102	  import untouched. This also disposes of the hindsight mojibake concern
103	  (`ef45a91ca`) entirely.
104	- **No `.gitignore`** (only `.hgignore`). `default_repository/caches/global.map`
105	  and `ProjectFortress/.dependencies/` are **not tracked** — both were
106	  added by the overlay. So the hindsight "untrack" items vanish; the
107	  hygiene commit *creates* a fresh `.gitignore` instead.
108	- **No tracked generated sources.** The graft first committed
109	  `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/` (~1,071 files), the four
110	  Rats!-generated parser `.java` files, `Library/FortressAst.{fsi,fss}`,
111	  and `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`. On the clean branch these are
112	  first committed at B4, freshly generated under the B2 determinism fixes.
113	- `bin/fortress_classpath` already exists at the base (the overlay only
114	  modified it).
115	- `ProjectFortress/demos/buffons.fss`, `Fortify/`, `README.txt`,
116	  `Specification/fortress.1.0.pdf` all present (kickoff README links and
117	  the PDF-commit deletion both resolve).
118	- The `tools.jar` pathelement in build.xml is **required** on JDK 8:
119	  `syntax_abstractions/rats/JavaC.java:39` calls
120	  `com.sun.tools.javac.Main.compile`, and every javac task has
121	  `includeantruntime="false"`. It stays through the whole base block and
122	  is dropped at R2 (JDK 11), where it dangles harmlessly.
123	
124	## Worktree and environment mechanics
125	
126	- Work in a second worktree sharing the same `.git`:
127	  `git worktree add ../fortress-clean a874948ac` then
128	  `cd /home/user/fortress-clean && git checkout -b clean-ladder`.
129	  The session cwd stays `/home/user/fortress`; the working-branch checkout
130	  is never disturbed mid-gate.
131	- All builds/gates run with `FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-clean` and
132	  `unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`. Env vars do not persist between shell calls —
133	  export them inside every command.
134	- JDKs (all verified installed): `/usr/lib/jvm/java-{8,11,17,21,25}-openjdk-amd64`.
135	  If the container was recycled, reinstall via
136	  `apt-get install -y openjdk-{8,11,17,21,25}-jdk-headless ant`.
137	- Disk is a fixed allowance: before starting, `ant clean` in
138	  `/home/user/fortress` and wipe its `default_repository/caches/*` to free
139	  space; do the same in the clean worktree between rungs if space runs low.
140	- Push: `git push -u origin clean-ladder` after the exhibit block, then
141	  after every gated commit (network retries per standing orders: 2s/4s/8s/16s).
142	- **Never** commit this plan, or any working-branch-only file, on
143	  `clean-ladder`. Never force-push `clean-ladder` once published except to
144	  fix a same-session mistake.
145	
146	## Orchestration (agreed with Pavol, 2026-08-23)
147	
148	Coordinator/worker split, so the coordinating session's context survives the
149	whole ladder without compaction:
150	
151	- **Coordinator** (the main session) never runs a build or reads a log dump.
152	  It sequences workers, launches them with a brief, and between workers runs
153	  cheap read-only verification: commit landed, tree matches the reference
154	  commit where this plan says it must, gate numbers as expected, checklist
155	  tick present. Deviations land with the coordinator; anything in "Known
156	  risks / stop conditions" goes to Pavol.
157	- **Workers** execute one step each, strictly **serially** (they share the
158	  `../fortress-clean` worktree). Each worker reads its step's section of
159	  this file directly — briefs point at the plan by reference (step ID, this
160	  file's path, worktree path, env constants, commit footer), they do not
161	  paraphrase it. Each worker: executes, verifies its own results, writes
162	  the commit(s) on `clean-ladder`, pushes at this plan's push points, ticks
163	  its checkbox in the Execution checklist below, commits that tick on the
164	  working branch, and reports back tersely (SHA, verification numbers,
165	  deviations).
166	- **Granularity**: E1–E6 and C1 are done inline by the coordinator (no
167	  builds, but concentrated fiddly judgment — cherry-pick conflict
168	  resolution, README edits); B1–B8 and R1–R8 get one worker per gated
169	  commit (the build/gate log volume is exactly what would force coordinator
170	  compaction).
171	- **Two branch tracks, never mixed**: rebuild commits exist only on
172	  `clean-ladder` (pushed to `origin/clean-ladder`; Pavol renames via the
173	  GitHub UI at the end; `main` is never touched from the clean worktree).
174	  Checklist ticks are working-branch commits in `/home/user/fortress` on
175	  `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr` — the ff-main standing order
176	  (`explorations/protocol.md` §4) applies to those pushes only.
177	
178	## Gate definitions
179	
180	- **Full gate**: `ant clean compileAll` + `ant testFast` + `ant testSystem`
181	  all green on the stated JDK, run in the clean worktree.
182	- **Cheap gate**: `ant compileAll` + `ant testFast` (used only where stated).
183	- Gate results (suite counts, JDK, wall time) go into the commit message of
184	  the gated commit — that is the project log.
185	- Until the speedup commit (B8) lands, testFast/testSystem run at 2012
186	  speed (slow; budget accordingly).
187	
188	## Commit sequence
189	
190	### Exhibit block (content from the working branch, no build claims)
191	
192	E1. **Kickoff README + hero SVGs.** New commit adding:
193	  - `README.md` — the approved README (working-branch `eb7e91859`
194	    version, which includes the linked implementation tour) with exactly
195	    one edit: in "Building, walking and running",
196	    the sentence "Fortress needs only a JDK and Apache Ant; the build has
197	    been kept working on modern JDKs." loses its second half — kickoff
198	    text: "Fortress needs only a JDK and Apache Ant." (The ladder hasn't
199	    happened yet at this point in history; the closing bookend C1 restores
200	    the clause.)
